news.title: AI refutes 30-year-old mathematical assumption in computer science
paras: “This came as a complete surprise, a shock,” says Fedor Fomin at the University of Bergen in Norway. Proposed nearly 30 years ago, the exponential time hypothesis (ETH) tries to put a limit on how quickly computers can solve certain logical puzzles.

The simplest way would be to try every possible combination of true or false for each part of the puzzle. ETH proposes that, although it may be possible to do this quicker with shortcuts, the amount of work needed has to grow exponentially as the puzzle gets bigger.

news.title: Clean-up underway as tens of thousands of homes left without power after Storm Boelo
paras: Storm Boelo battered parts of the north of England, Northern Ireland and Scotland this weekend, and as of 7pm on Sunday night, 90,000 homes were still without power according to the Energy Network Agency. Winds of 85mph were recorded on Saturday, and the high winds caused lots of damage in affected areas.

Published 1 September Boelo came soon after Storm Austen brought strong winds and heavy rain on Friday, leaving many homes in the South West of England without power. An amber warning for wind was in place for Scotland, parts of Northern Ireland and parts of northern England on Saturday and Sunday.

news.title: 'I didn't know our great-grandma did such amazing things'
paras: Well, Press Packers Elise and Renae's great-grandmother Locita Brandy has won a Manchester University Medal of Honour. She was one of the founders of the Manchester Caribbean Carnival and also fought against racism in education.

The award is for her community work and for many years campaigning to help black children. The sisters went to interview Locita for Newsround to find out more about her life and how she improved things for many black children. They discovered some of her achievements, like changing school dinners, leading Saturday school so kids from the Caribbean could learn about their heritage, and getting books with racist language removed from the school library.

news.title: Tanzania celebrates first natural gas discovery in more than 10 years
paras: Tanzania has announced a significant discovery of natural gas in the Mnazi Bay area in the south of the country - the first such find in a decade.

Energy Minister Juma Homera attended a ceremony at the Kasa-1X ST2 well, which is jointly owned by state-owned Tanzania Petroleum Development Corporation (TPDC) and French oil firm Maurel & Prom, to mark the occasion. He said the estimated 223 billion cubic feet (6.3 billion cubic metres) discovery was a "major milestone" in the development of the small oil and gas sector in the East African nation.

paras: A bust-up between mathematicians is fuelling fears that AI could undermine science Inside: dozens of small boxes with barcoded glass tubes, collectively containing one hundred billion genes. news.title: Nanotyrannus skeleton sells for $47.3m in New York auction
paras: The mounted skeleton of a newly-identified dinosaur once mistaken for a young Tyrannosaurus rex has sold at auction for a colossal $47.3m (£35.5m). Nicknamed Jodi, the roughly 10-foot-tall (3m) skeleton was auctioned by Sotheby's in New York. The sale comes a year after researchers confirmed that the skeleton belongs to a distinct genus.

The Late Cretaceous carnivore was expected to fetch at least $9m when it went under the hammer on Tuesday. The auction comes after Sotheby's sold a Tyrannosaurus rex, dubbed Gus, for a record $50.1m in July. The sale has reignited debate in the scientific community over whether dinosaur remains should be sold privately or displayed publicly.

news.title: Ceasefire extended across Ukraine's Kherson region, officials say
paras: A ceasefire that began with the aim of getting food and medicine to the Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky has been extended across the wider southern region of Kherson, according to sources. Several thousand residents are trapped in the city with no access to food, water and electricity.

On one side is the Dnipro river, while Russian forces are on the other and all the roads out are too dangerous. However, no breaches of the truce that began early on Tuesday have so far been reported. US First Lady Melania Trump, who helped broker the ceasefire along with Pope Leo XIV, said on Tuesday that the area involved had been expanded to provide "safe passage" for humanitarian convoys.

news.title: Is Taekwondo an art or A Sport?
paras: And then… silence, and then someone from the crowd shouted… “Is Taekwondo a sport or is it a performing arts?” Well we are here to answer that question! Did you know that Taekwondo is Korean? In Korean, chung and hung mean blue and red.

sport.title: Stan Wawrinka: The Other Swiss Tennis Great From The Big Four Era
paras: Trying to make your name in a sport dominated by a select few players was a challenge Stan Wawrinka seemed to relish. The Big Four were Roger Federer, Rafael Nadal, Andy Murray, and Novak Djokovic. Between 2004 and 2023, they won 69 of the 79 Grand Slams held.

During this period, only one player outside of the quartet won a major three times – Wawrinka. On his way to the 2014 Australian Open title, he defeated both Djokovic and Nadal, as well as three other seeded players. The following year, he defeated Federer and Djokovic to win the French Open.
